description: THE TABLES OF ONE ACT: for each, its handle, title, where it sits in the act, how many rows and columns it has, its column names and its first rows. Use it first when an act holds a classification, a chart of accounts, a tariff, a list of products or any annex that is a table: get_act_structure lists articles and divisions, not tables. Then read a table with read_table or search inside it with search_tables. It also says what the act holds that is NOT text and cannot be read here (drawings and pictures).

law.description: The act that holds the tables, however it is at hand: a citation ('ORDIN 337/2007', 'OMFP 1802/2014'), a common name ('Codul fiscal') or a title any tool printed.

offset.description: Tables to skip (the answer says what to send for the next page).

part.description: Optional. Only the tables whose title or place in the act contains this text, diacritics ignored, e.g. 'anexa 2' or 'plan de conturi'.

name: list_tables
